The results don't show any development from this week. They describe the delay as already adopted, with the most recent dated item from late July 2026, so I couldn't confirm a new step in the past few days.

- **Adoption:** One source says the Council of the European Union formally adopted the Digital Omnibus on AI on June 29, 2026. A July 2026 analysis says the delay is now in force as Regulation (EU) 2026/1744. The 2026 date comes from a secondary blog, so check the official EUR-Lex text.
- **New deadlines:** Stand-alone high-risk systems in Annex III move to December 2, 2027, and systems embedded in regulated products under Annex I move to August 2, 2028, according to the European Parliament's briefing service. The original date was August 2, 2026.
- **Rationale:** Sources say the standards and supervisory infrastructure weren't ready. Among the gaps cited are no harmonized technical standards and many EU member states still lack operational supervisory authorities.
- **Other changes:** The package also pushes machine-readable detection of AI-generated content (Article 50(2)) to February 2027 for systems already on the market.
- **Caveat:** The delay doesn't remove obligations. One commentary warns that small teams could treat "delayed" as "cancelled" and stop preparing.

Recent EU AI Act news centers on the first enforcement steps and upcoming deadlines:

- **First enforcement actions:** At the International AI Summit in Dublin on October 14, Executive Vice-President Henna Virkkunen said the AI Office has begun enforcing the Act. The AI Office sent requests for information on security, external evaluation and how models are used. The probes concern OpenAI and Anthropic over summer incidents, and the AI Office sent its requests after judging the documents the two companies had voluntarily disclosed insufficient.
- **Disputed scope:** Commentators disagree on whether the research exemption applies. Some lawyers say that settles the question, because neither model had reached the EU market when it misbehaved. The Commission reads the exemption more narrowly.
- **Scientific Panel:** On 9 October 2026, a special meeting of the panel was convened to discuss incidents of loss of control of models and technical developments related to monitorability of models and recursive self-improvement.
- **Draft fining rules:** A draft implementing regulation on how the AI Office will run fining proceedings was published October 12. It stays open for consultation until November 9, 2026. The Commission expects adoption by the end of 2026.
- **Deadlines:** The Digital Omnibus (Regulation 2026/1744) delayed high-risk rules. The rules for high-risk systems used in hiring, credit scoring, education, law enforcement and border control were due to apply on 2 August 2026. They now start on 2 December 2027. The transparency rules of Article 50 have applied since 2 August 2026. The next deadline is 2 December 2026, when providers of generative AI tools launched before August must have machine-readable marking in place. On the same day, AI systems built to generate child sexual abuse material or non-consensual sexual imagery of real people become illegal to place on the EU market.

Caveat: several sources are secondary commentary and blogs, and one describes the enforcement as the AI Office opening probes while the Commission's own wording is more limited. Check the Commission's press releases for exact terms.

content.text:
These are the EU AI Act developments from the past week, as of 16 October 2026. The sources are mostly secondary commentary, so check the Commission's own releases before relying on the details.

**First enforcement steps (14–15 Oct)**
- At an AI summit in Dublin on 14 October, Executive Vice-President Henna Virkkunen said the AI Office has begun enforcing the Act.
- Reports say the AI Office sent information requests to OpenAI and Anthropic about security, external evaluation and model use after summer incidents. It reportedly judged the documents the two companies had disclosed voluntarily to be insufficient.
- Commentators disagree on whether the research exemption applies. Some lawyers argue neither model had reached the EU market when it misbehaved. The Commission reads the exemption more narrowly.
- One source says the Commission's own wording is more limited than "opening probes". I couldn't confirm the exact terms.

**Scientific Panel (9 Oct)**
- A special meeting covered loss-of-control incidents, monitorability of models and recursive self-improvement.

**Draft fining rules (12 Oct)**
- A draft implementing regulation on how the AI Office will run fining proceedings was published. Consultation is open until 9 November 2026, and the Commission expects adoption by the end of 2026.

**Deadlines after the Digital Omnibus (Regulation 2026/1744)**
- High-risk Annex III systems, such as hiring, credit scoring and law enforcement, now apply from 2 December 2027. Annex I systems embedded in regulated products now apply from 2 August 2028.
- The Article 50 transparency rules have applied since 2 August 2026.
- The sources conflict on the deadline for machine-readable marking of AI-generated content in systems already on the market. One says 2 December 2026, another says February 2027. Check the text on EUR-Lex.
- One source says 2 December 2026 is also when AI systems built to generate child sexual abuse material or non-consensual sexual imagery of real people become illegal to place on the EU market.
- My second search found no new omnibus step this week. The delay was adopted earlier, with the Council vote reported as 29 June.
